alex_k: Hey — onboarding RW-NOVA-12B weights to hosted. I ran the convert script to safetensors and sharded for TP=4 but samples look corrupted after ~256 tokens (repeated tokens / sudden strange ids). Command I ran:

```bash
python tools/convert_ckpt.py --src s3://redwood-models/rw-nova/pt-checkpoints/step-350k --dst s3://redwood-models/rw-nova/safetensors/tp4/ --dtype bf16 --tp 4 --shard-mode tp_split --keep-ckpt --config config.json
```

Files are at s3://redwood-models/rw-nova/safetensors/tp4/{model-0000-of-0004.safetensors,...}. Local quick-check: `python -c "from rw_infer import load_model; m=load_model('s3://.../model', device='cpu'); print(m.generate('Hello'))"` -> garbage.

I suspect either: shard ordering mismatch (tp axis ordering) OR tokenizer merged/added tokens mismatch (token ids off). Any quick checks before I start re-converting? :eyes:

maria_s: Did you compare the base vocab/id mapping? If the tokenizer saved added_tokens.json or special_tokens_map.json got changed, you can get "off by N" token ids. Check `tokenizer.get_vocab()` vs original. Also confirm config.json `vocab_size` and `use_fast_tokenizer` match.

jong_w: For TP shard ordering, we historically have two layouts: contiguous TP shards (split on embed dim) vs interleaved/stride layout (used by some export tools). Quick check: load the first tensor of lm_head weights and sum across shards to see if shapes align. Example:

```python
import safetensors as st
from safetensors import safe_open
# open a shard and inspect keys/shapes
with safe_open('model-0000-of-0004.safetensors', framework='pt') as f:
    for k in f.keys():
        print(k, f.get_tensor(k).shape)
```

If shapes are unexpected (e.g., world_size dim collapsed), the converter likely used wrong axis.

alex_k: Good call. I looked at lm_head weight shapes — each shard has [32000, 3072] (vocab, hidden) which seems right, but when I sum softmax inputs we still get repeated tokens. I also found that the original tokenizer had 3 custom added tokens; the converter script appended them at the end which shifted ids by +3 compared to the saved PT tokenizer.

tasha: Two things to try: 1) Re-run conversion with `--preserve-tokenizer` (flag we added last month) which will copy tokenizer files verbatim instead of rebuilding. 2) For TP layout, try `--tp-layout legacy` vs `--tp-layout contiguous` — the CLI supports both. Also run `tools/validate_pack.py --model-dir <s3 path>`; it runs a small gen test and checksum comparisons.

alex_k: Re-ran with `--preserve-tokenizer` and `--tp-layout contiguous`. New shards uploaded to s3://redwood-models/rw-nova/safetensors/tp4-contiguous/. Ran `tools/validate_pack.py` -> it failed with `KV_CACHE_KEY_MISMATCH` in logs. snippet:

```
ERROR: KV_CACHE_KEY_MISMATCH: expected 'present_key_0' found 'presentk_0' in shard 0002
```

Does that mean param key naming changed between conversion steps? Any history of renaming (present_key vs presentk)?

jong_w: Yeah we had a subtle bug in the converter where we strip underscores in key names for legacy exports. CI caught it last week for one model. Quick fix: run `python tools/fix_keys.py --src <shard-dir> --pattern 'presentk_' --replace 'present_key_'` which will rewrite safetensors keys in-place (creates .bak). Then re-run validate.

ci-bot: Build 5321 triggered: validate_pack.py on rw-nova (tp4-contiguous) -> FAILED. Logs: https://ci.redwood/5321/logs (KV_CACHE_KEY_MISMATCH).

maria_s: Also check `config.json` field `rotary_dim` and `rope_scaling`. If those are wrong, generation will degrade after certain token lengths (like ~256). That matches your symptom. The tokenizer shift explains initial token mismatch too. Both combined could make output look "garbled" after a threshold.

alex_k: Thanks — ran fix_keys.py, revalidated, now validate_pack passes locally. Pushed the new manifest and updated hosted model metadata to point to tp4-contiguous. CI build re-run queued.

tasha: Nice. One more note for the docs: add a short checklist entry about preserving tokenizer files and `--tp-layout` options + the key-fix utility. I can PR to the model-onboarding playbook. :+1:

alex_k: Will do a tiny PR. Thanks y'all. If CI passes I'll promote to canary tomorrow.
